correctness.rationale: The finite-dimensional lossy semigroup splits into the maximal adjacency-invariant dark subspace in ker Gamma and its orthogonal cyclic complement. The complete cyclic space from all weight-one absorbers is exactly the radial shell representation except the unique even-dimension central Krawtchouk eigenvector, plus the standard coordinate representation on every interior shell. The centered-incidence tight-frame identity gives all matrix entries of the orthogonal projector. Positive loss at every absorbing site ensures strict decay on the complement; no finite-test extrapolation is used. Exact rational independent-formula checks match 21,840 matrix entries in dimensions two through seven and six finite-field Krylov ranks.

originality.rationale: The novelty is the **full position-basis coherent capture effect operator** for an entire weight-one absorbing layer and its all-initial-state functional. Previously available all-radius Hamming-sphere bright rank formulas and single-corner survival results are expressly excluded as new assertions. Projector rank and one diagonal entry do not imply the remaining matrix entries, the even-parity cross-shell rank-one coupling, or the phase-controlled antipodal capture law. Inspected trapping/hypercube sources and the two close published Fourier-concentration results concern either general mechanisms or different operators. Residual risk is an unlocated equivalent result in Bose–Mesner/Terwilliger or observability literature; search evidence cannot prove worldwide priority.
residual_risks: An algebraically equivalent capture projector may appear in unlocated earlier Terwilliger-algebra, association-scheme, or quantum-network controllability work.

value.rationale: A natural spatial detector pattern on the Boolean cube has a fully explicit quantum-capture effect operator, allowing exact probabilities for arbitrary coherent/mixed preparations rather than only the dimension of capturable modes. The even-versus-odd collapse of cross-shell coherences is structural; for \(Q_4\), relative-phase change between two opposite corners produces capture 1/4 versus 1 even though single-corner capture is always 5/8. The complete operator is directly reusable for preparation optimization and detector design in an ideal coherent network, despite no finite-time noise claim.
